title: Chain rule

source_policy: Definition-level references support the mathematical vocabulary. All stories and worked quantities are original constructed teaching scenarios, not measurements or historical events. Historical priority and notation claims require separate claim-level evidence before publication.
purpose: Follow a small change through an inner rule and an outer rule.
meaning: For a differentiable composition, the local sensitivity is the outer derivative evaluated at the inner output, multiplied by the inner derivative. In the live example an affine calibration selects a side and the square rule turns it into area. The chain rule tracks how a setting change reaches that area.

definition.setting: Real functions with compatible local domains: g is differentiable at x and f is differentiable at g(x). The executable specimen is a square after an affine rule, with bounded real controls.
definition.formal_latex: h=f\circ g,\quad h(x)=f(g(x)),\quad h'(x)=f'(g(x))g'(x).\quad g(x)=ax+b,\ f(u)=u^2,\ u=g(x)\Rightarrow h'(x)=2(ax+b)a.

signature.x,a,b: Finite real controls; x in [-3,3], a in [-2,2], b in [-3,3].
signature.h′(x): chainDerivative, the primary scalar output; expandedDerivative gives an algebraically expanded check.

conditions: For the general chain rule, g is differentiable at x and f is differentiable at g(x), with the composition defined in the relevant neighborhood.
The inner slope is evaluated at x; the outer slope is evaluated at the current inner value u=g(x).
The restricted live family is g(x)=a*x+b and f(u)=u². Their composition h(x)=(a*x+b)² is differentiable for every real x.
Derivative products describe local first-order sensitivity; a finite input change need not produce exactly derivative times that change.
Physical story units are declared separately. A panel-side interpretation requires a positive finished side; signed polynomial inputs remain valid mathematics outside that interpretation.
definition.domain_notes: The general chain rule applies to differentiable compatible functions, beyond polynomials and beyond this one-variable example. The live UI is restricted to f(u)=u² and g(x)=a*x+b with bounded real controls. It is not a symbolic differentiator or an arbitrary function editor. Negative inner values remain valid polynomial inputs; a physical square-side story uses positive sides and compatible units. No finite-step quotient is substituted for the exact analytic derivative.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level reference; worked properties are author-derived for stated assumptions. Independent mathematical review pending.

grammar.expression_latex: h=f\circ g,\quad h(x)=f(g(x)),\quad h'(x)=f'(g(x))g'(x).\quad g(x)=ax+b,\ f(u)=u^2,\ u=g(x)\Rightarrow h'(x)=2(ax+b)a.
grammar.precedence: Evaluate g(x)=ax+b first. Evaluate f and its derivative at the current inner value u=g(x), then multiply the outer derivative by g′(x). Parentheses identify function arguments and preserve the composition order.

nodes.ref: Derivative of the square map: a real input is multiplied by 2

scopes.domain_condition: The live square-after-affine family is defined and differentiable for all real controls; UI controls remain within their declared finite bounds.

parse_errors.input: Evaluate f′ at x instead of g(x)
parse_errors.reason: The outer function receives u=g(x), so its derivative factor is f′(g(x)).

parse_errors.input: Add the stage derivatives instead of multiplying them
parse_errors.reason: For a differentiable composition the chain rule multiplies the correctly evaluated local derivative factors.

parse_errors.input: Call a finite output change exactly h′(x) times the input change for every step
parse_errors.reason: That equality is generally only a first-order local approximation, not an exact finite-change identity.

grammar.ast_coverage: The tree explicitly forms the inner value, applies the outer square map and its derivative, then multiplies the outer derivative by the inner coefficient a. The root is the composite derivative, not the composed value. The general differentiability theorem is stated separately; this tree describes the restricted analytic family.

properties.conditions: g(x)=ax+b and f(u)=u² with real a,b,x.
properties.derivation: Apply the square derivative at u=ax+b and multiply by the affine derivative a; independent expansion gives the same polynomial derivative.
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent review pending

properties.claim: A zero composite derivative at one point does not imply a constant composite function.
properties.derivation: h(x)=(x-1)² has h′(1)=0, but h(1+ε)=ε² differs from h(1) when ε≠0.
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent review pending

examples.title: Trace setting sensitivity into panel area
examples.question: At x=1 m, the drawing tool uses a=2 and b=1 m. How quickly does panel area change with the setting?

The calibration factor a is dimensionless and offset b is measured in metres; the outer rule f(u)=u² gives square area in m².
Values and calibration rules are stipulated examples, not measurements of a real machine.

steps.reason: The current setting first determines the finished side, then its square area.

prompts.prompt: Where should the outer slope be evaluated?
prompts.answer: At u=g(x), the value actually supplied to the outer function, rather than at the original x.

prompts.prompt: Does multiplying two derivatives predict an arbitrary finite change exactly?
prompts.answer: No. The derivative is local first-order sensitivity; nonlinear finite changes need the full function calculation.
